```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5.5, dpi = 120)
source("../R/_load.R")
```

This notebook reads the DHS Women's Individual Recode (IR) file, builds the analysis variables defined in `R/data_prep.R`, documents the sample flow and the missing data, and saves the analysis dataset for the other notebooks. All variable names come from `config/config.yml`, so a different KDHS round only needs a new configuration file.

```{r read}
raw <- read_dhs_ir(cfg$paths$data, config_vars(cfg))
df  <- build_analysis_data(raw, cfg)
saveRDS(df, file.path(cfg$paths$out, "data", "analysis_data.rds"))
dim(raw)
```

## Sample flow (STROBE item 13)

```{r flow}
flow <- sample_flow(df); save_table(flow, "01_sample_flow", cfg)
knitr::kable(flow, digits = 0, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Missing data

Structural missingness (for example, decision-making is not asked of women outside a union) is kept as an explicit category, so it is shown separately from true missing values.

```{r missing}
miss <- missingness_table(df, cfg); save_table(miss, "01_missingness", cfg)
knitr::kable(miss)
```

## Outcomes

```{r outcomes}
prev <- overall_prevalence(df, cfg); save_table(prev, "01_overall_prevalence", cfg)
knitr::kable(prev, digits = 2)
```

## Sample characteristics

```{r table1}
t1 <- sample_characteristics(df, c(cfg$analysis$covariates, "timing")); save_table(t1, "01_sample_characteristics", cfg)
knitr::kable(t1, digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```
